explore.line: The lobby gear came from the tower's very first lift. It still turns.
notes: Gears pass a turn along. When one gear turns, the gear touching it turns the other way.
The big gear has no off switch. It just likes spinning.
explore.fact: The big gear in the lobby came from the tower's first lift.

explore.line: The front desk. Visitors sign in here before they ride the lift.
notes: Today's visitors: two engineers, one robot and zero dinosaurs.
The desk bell goes ding. Lifty loves the ding.
explore.fact: Visitors sign in at the front desk.

explore.line: The workshop toolbox. Every tool has its own place, so nothing gets lost.
notes: Engineers clean their tools after every job, so they are ready for the next one.
The crew counts the tools at the end of the day. All here!
explore.fact: In the workshop toolbox every tool has its own place.

explore.line: Utility. This valve lets water into the pipes. Watch the gauge needle move.
notes: Turn a valve one way to open it, and the other way to close it.
Water pushes on the pipes. The gauge shows how hard it pushes.
explore.fact: A valve opens and closes a pipe. The gauge shows how hard the water pushes.

explore.line: A toy robot! Someone lost it down here. Its wind-up spring still works.
notes: Its name tag says TIN. Nobody knows who TIN belongs to.
Wind-up toys need no batteries. Turning the key gives them their power.
explore.fact: A wind-up toy has a spring inside. Turning the key winds the spring up.

explore.line: Storage. The crew's long hose lives on this reel, rolled up so it never tangles.
notes: A hose on a reel is quick to pull out and easy to put away.
The crew once pulled the whole hose out. It reached all the way to the lift.
explore.fact: A long hose is kept rolled up on a reel, so it never gets tangled.

explore.line: Small parts are sorted into these bins. Each kind has a bin of its own.
notes: Bolts, nuts and washers each get a bin of their own.
One bin says MYSTERY PARTS. Nobody opens that one.
explore.fact: Small parts are sorted into bins, one kind in each, so they are quick to find.

explore.line: Ventilation level. These fans move air through the whole building.
notes: Fresh air comes in and old air goes out. The fans keep it moving.
The fans spin faster on hot days to keep the tower cool.
explore.fact: These fans move fresh air through the building.

explore.line: The fan switch. Engineers turn the fans off here before they fix them.
notes: The switch has two words on it: ON and OFF.
Switch off, then fix. That rule keeps engineers safe.
explore.fact: Engineers switch a machine off before they work on it.

explore.line: Machine room. This motor turns the big wheel that pulls our lift's cables.
notes: The lift's cables wrap around a grooved wheel. The motor turns that wheel.
A heavy weight on the other end of the cables helps the motor lift the car.
explore.fact: The motor turns a wheel called a sheave. The sheave moves the cables that lift the car.

explore.line: Platform heights. The springs push the platforms back up after every jump.
notes: Squash a spring and it pushes back. That push makes the platforms bounce.
Boing! The springs never get tired of jumping.
explore.fact: Springs on the platform heights push back up when they are pressed down.

explore.line: The test lab. Each flask lights up when its test is running.
notes: Every test in the lab is written down, so nobody forgets what happened.
One flask bubbles every time someone tells a joke.
explore.fact: In the test lab, new parts are tried out before they go into the tower.

explore.line: The monitor draws a wave. It shows how a part shakes while it is tested.
notes: A big wave means a big shake. A flat line means everything is still.
Engineers test each part so the lift rides smooth and quiet.
explore.fact: A test lab monitor draws a wave to show how a part moves.

explore.line: The wind ruins. This old windmill still turns whenever the wind blows.
notes: A windmill turns the push of the wind into turning power.
Its sails catch the wind, like the sail on a boat.
explore.fact: The old windmill in the wind ruins turns when the wind blows.

explore.line: An old banner from the wind ruins. It still flaps in the breeze.
notes: Watch the banner to see which way the wind blows.
The banner has flown up here so long, the birds know it.
explore.fact: A banner shows which way the wind is blowing.

explore.line: Relay room. When someone presses a call button, a relay clicks and its lamp comes on.
notes: A relay is a switch that another switch can turn on.
Click, click, click. Each click is someone calling the lift.
explore.fact: Relays are switches. They pass each call from a floor along to the lift.

explore.line: The big dial. Its pointer sweeps round to show how many calls are waiting.
notes: When the pointer is low, the lift is not busy.
On very busy days the pointer swings almost all the way round.
explore.fact: The big dial in the relay room shows how many calls are waiting.

explore.line: Comms room. Message from the roof: the golf course is open today.
notes: Message from the plant floor: the tomatoes are ready to pick.
Message from the workshop: who borrowed the big wrench?
explore.fact: The comms room sends messages between the floors of the tower.

explore.line: The radio dish catches messages from far away.
notes: The dish is shaped like a bowl to gather radio waves.
Today the dish heard a weather report and one very loud bird.
explore.fact: A radio dish is curved so it can catch faint signals.

explore.line: Engineering bay. The gantry crane lifts heavy lift parts and carries them across the room.
notes: A gantry crane runs on rails high above the floor.
The crane can lift a whole lift car. Gently, of course.
explore.fact: In the engineering bay, a gantry crane rolls along a beam and lifts heavy parts.

explore.line: A new pulley wheel for a lift. The lift's cables run in the groove around its rim.
notes: A pulley wheel helps a cable change direction.
The groove keeps the cable from slipping off the wheel.
explore.fact: A lift's cables run around a pulley wheel. The crew builds and fixes them here.

explore.line: Block builder. The crane lowers each block into place, one at a time.
notes: Cranes lower their loads slowly, so nothing bumps.
The crane driver says: up a bit, down a bit, perfect!
explore.fact: The crane on the block builder lowers blocks into place one at a time.

explore.line: High service, high up in the tower. This lamp lights the ladder the crew climbs to the machines above.
notes: The crew climbs up here to check the machines above the lift.
The lamp sways a little when the wind blows outside.
explore.fact: High service is high up in the tower. Its ladder goes up to a hatch in the ceiling.

explore.line: Safety cones mark a spot to keep clear while the crew works.
notes: Cones are bright so everyone can spot them from far away.
The cones take turns standing guard.
explore.fact: Bright cones warn people to keep away from a work area.

explore.line: Primary power. The core is running again. That's the power you restored.
notes: The core sends power down cables to every floor.
The core hums when it is happy. It is very happy now.
explore.fact: This core sends power to the floors of the building, and to our lift.

explore.line: Hydroponics. The grow lights shine like sunshine, so plants can grow inside the tower.
notes: Plants use light to make their own food.
The lights are on a timer, so the plants get a night too.
explore.fact: Grow lights give indoor plants the light they need to grow.

explore.line: These plants grow without soil. The crew gives them water with plant food in it.
notes: Their roots drink straight from the water.
The crew grows lettuce up here. Crunchy!
explore.fact: In hydroponics, plants grow without soil, in water with plant food mixed in.

explore.line: The archive. The building's plans live in these drawers.
notes: A plan is a drawing of a building, seen from above.
Every pipe and wire in the tower is drawn on a plan.
explore.fact: The building's plans are kept here. Some drawings show places we have not been yet.

card.title: The Tower Book
lines: This tower has twenty floors, from the lobby up to the roof.
Our lift rides up and down one tall shaft.
Strong steel cables hold the car, and a big wheel moves them.

explore.line: The tower book. Here is a page about our lift.
notes: The book has a page for every floor of the tower.
Someone drew a smiley face in the corner of a page.
explore.fact: The archive's tower book tells how the lift moves up and down.

explore.line: The observatory. From up here you can see how high the tower reaches.
notes: A telescope uses lenses to make far things look close.
On clear nights the crew looks at the moon from here.
explore.fact: From the observatory you can see how high the tower reaches.

explore.line: The star chart shows which stars to look for tonight.
notes: Stars that make a picture together are called constellations.
Someone drew a tiny Lifty in the corner of the chart.
explore.fact: A star chart is a map of the night sky.

explore.line: The sky bridge joins two parts of the tower. This far door leads into the other part.
notes: The bridge is strong enough for the whole crew at once.
Knock, knock. The far door opens when that part of the tower is ready.
explore.fact: The sky bridge joins two parts of the tower, high above the city.

explore.line: Up here the wind is strong, so it turns the little turbine fast.
notes: A wind turbine turns the push of the wind into electricity.
The faster the wind blows, the faster the turbine spins.
explore.fact: A wind turbine turns in the wind. The turning makes electric power.

explore.line: Rooftop golf, at the very top of the tower. The ball rolls right to the hole.
notes: Golf balls have little dents called dimples. They help the ball fly.
Hole in one! Well, the ball did most of the work.
explore.fact: The rooftop golf course is on Floor 20, the very top of the tower.
